source.title: Sequence-to-sequence pretraining for a less-resourced Slovenian language

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates Slovene T5 models at different sizes and pretraining durations on downstream tasks, extending scale-related evaluation to a new language and model setting. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream task scores for its Slovene models at different sizes and training durations, which bear on V6. It does not report held-out pretraining loss, a power-law fit, or predictions from smaller runs. Its discussion of compute allocation uses downstream task scores and does not test loss-minimising allocation. Results for multilingual comparator models are left out of the rows; the rows focus on the study's own size/training sweep.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own Slovene T5 models at two sizes (60M, 750M) and several pretraining lengths (1, 3, 5 epochs), then compares fine-tuned downstream scores. That bears on V6 (downstream gains with scale) in a new language and architecture. It reports no pretraining loss, no fits and no extrapolation, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested. Its equal-compute comparison uses downstream scores, not loss, so it does not test V3 as worded. The test of V6 is weak: only two sizes, no fitted relation, no uncertainty.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors find SloT5 lags BERT-like models on classification but is useful for generation. Large models beat small ones at the same training amount, with modest SloT5 gaps. More training helps the small model a lot; for the large model, gains are modest, mostly between 1 and 3 epochs, and the 3 vs 5 epoch difference is negligible. Because small5 beats large1 at equal compute, the optimal tokens/parameter ratio must exceed 5. They attribute the weak large model to insufficient training data.
record.recipe_differences: Downstream benchmark evaluation of Slovene encoder-decoder models across model sizes and pretraining durations; no held-out pretraining-loss sweep or power-law fitting.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported size and training-duration trends vary by downstream task; for large SloT5 models, the authors say the difference between 1, 3, and 5 epochs depends on the task.

fits_no_version.finding: T5-sl-small5 and T5-sl-large1 used roughly equal compute; small5 (414 tokens/param) beats large1 (5.5 tokens/param) on most downstream tasks. The authors conclude the optimal ratio exceeds 5 for Slovene T5, citing Hoffmann et al.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed compute, a smaller model trained on more tokens outperforms a larger under-trained one on downstream tasks (a downstream analogue of compute-optimal allocation).

record.problems: No held-out pretraining loss, scaling-law fit, or uncertainty estimates are reported. Downstream generative-task ROUGE-L scores are noted by the authors to be imperfect indicators of human-rated quality.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for multilingual mT5 and mBART comparators, BERT-like models, and majority-class baselines in Tables 4–5 were omitted to keep the catalog focused on the study's own Slovene model size/training sweep within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: There is no fitted or predictive relation, no link to pretraining loss, only two model sizes, and no uncertainty estimates.
No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit.
No loss-minimising split. The equal-compute comparison uses downstream scores only.
No loss scaling in other regimes.

missing.what: Tokens-per-parameter ratios for each model (5.5, 20, 33, 68, 414) and the statement that small5 and large1 used roughly equal compute

Majority-class baselines (BoolQ 63.3, CB 21.7, COPA 50.0, RTE 58.6, WSC 65.8, NER 0.0, SA 20.3) belong in the baseline field of the classification rows; without them the near-chance results cannot be read

record.verdict_notes: The reader's states were inconsistent: identical values got different states, and the smallest model's rows were marked observed with no comparison. I re-coded states relative to the appropriate smaller or less-trained SloT5 model, and treated small1 rows as references (cannot_determine). Many SuperGLUE scores sit at or below majority class, so they are weak evidence either way. This is a model-release paper whose scale comparison spans only two sizes, so the V6 evidence is thin.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss measurements or power-law fits in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No predictions of larger-run losses from fits to smaller runs.

Although the paper compares models trained with different token/parameter ratios and discusses equal-compute runs, it does not measure held-out loss or determine a loss-minimising split as a function of compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No tests of the same loss scaling form in other modalities or training regimes.
No pretraining-loss-to-downstream-performance relation is measured, and no predictive law is fitted; downstream scores are compared across the tested Slovene models and tasks.
No scaling exponents are fitted or compared, and no curves are analyzed for bending away from a power law.

relationships.condition: Generative tasks (lemmatization, summarization) plus NER and RTE, comparing SloT5 small vs large and 1 vs 3/5 epochs
relationships.reason: Scores rise with size and with training, e.g. lemmatization sentence accuracy 37.1→58.5→72.2 (r37, r41, r43). Other gains: r08, r10, r17, r19, r20, r27–r29, r32, r38–r43, r45, r47, r49, r50, r52, r53.
relationships.display_finding: Scores increased with model size and training duration, including lemmatization sentence accuracy of 37.1→58.5→72.2.

relationships.condition: SuperGLUE reasoning tasks (COPA, BoolQ, WSC), text simplification at equal steps, and extra training of the large model
relationships.reason: COPA stays at chance at every size (r12–r15). BoolQ and WSC fall with more training (r04, r05, r25). Large1 scores below small1 on text simplification (r58). Large3 vs large5 is task-dependent and negligible (r30, r44, r55). Gains on SA and summarization are small (r33–r35, r48, r54).
relationships.display_finding: COPA stayed at chance, BoolQ and WSC declined with more training, the larger model underperformed on simplification, and additional training offered negligible or small gains elsewhere.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SloT5 models across the reported downstream tasks and training durations
reader_labels.reason: Outcomes vary by task and duration: the paper says additional large-model training does not always help and the better large checkpoint depends on the task; see r04-r05, r14-r15, r24-r25, r29-r30, r44, r50, r55, and r59-r60. The study does not fit a predictive relation.
